## `lakana.asset`

Signature: `lakana.asset(function: object = None, /, *, inputs: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, description: str | None = None, label: str | None = None, owner: str | None = None, tags: Iterable[str] = (), materialize: str | None = None, columns: Mapping[str, str | Mapping[str, str]] | None = None, retries: int | None = None, retry_delay: int | str | None = None, timeout: int | str | None = None, output: str = 'table', keep_versions: int | None = None, decimals: str = 'float', connections: Iterable[str] = (), write: str = 'replace', key: Iterable[str] | str = (), watermark: str | None = None, evolve_schema: bool | None = False, valid_from: str | None = None, close_missing: bool | None = None, kind: str | None = None, grain: str | None = None, references: Mapping[str, str | Mapping[str, str]] | None = None, checks: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, measures: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None = None, health: str | bool | Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> Callable[[F], F]`

Declare a Python asset; returns the function unchanged with its metadata attached.

Every argument must be a literal in the source file: deploy reads the decorator without running the file.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `function` | `object` | `None` | Never pass this. It only catches a bare ``@asset``. |
| `inputs` | `Mapping[str, str] | None` | `None` | Parameter name → dotted table name. |
| `description` | `str | None` | `None` | Human description. |
| `label` | `str | None` | `None` | A short name for the table in the project's main language: one line, at most 100 characters. |
| `owner` | `str | None` | `None` | Owning team or person. |
| `tags` | `Iterable[str]` | `()` | Free-form tags. |
| `materialize` | `str | None` | `None` | ``table`` (the only supported value); not allowed with ``output="artifact"``. An asset that appends says ``write="append"`` instead. |
| `columns` | `Mapping[str, str | Mapping[str, str]] | None` | `None` | Column name → its description, or `{"label": ..., "description": ...}`. |
| `retries` | `int | None` | `None` | Retries after a failed attempt. |
| `retry_delay` | `int | str | None` | `None` | First retry delay. |
| `timeout` | `int | str | None` | `None` | Wall-clock limit of one attempt. |
| `output` | `str` | `'table'` | ``table`` (the default): the function returns a `polars.DataFrame` that becomes the table. ``artifact``: the function writes files into `output_dir` and returns a path inside it; each run stores one new, numbered version of the artifact, which another asset can read. |
| `keep_versions` | `int | None` | `None` | Only with ``output="artifact"``: how many live versions to keep, from 1 to 2147483647. After each run the oldest versions beyond it are deleted. Leave it out to keep every version. |
| `decimals` | `str` | `'float'` | ``float`` (the default): a SQL ``DECIMAL`` column of an input reaches the function as a ``Float64`` column, so ``value * 0.5`` works; decimals inside lists and structs too. ``exact``: it arrives as a ``Decimal`` column of ``decimal.Decimal`` values, for money or any calculation that must not round. A float holds about 15 significant digits, so with ``float`` a value beyond 2**53 or with more digits arrives rounded, without an error: use ``exact`` for a decimal identifier or a wide sum. What the function returns is stored as it is. |
| `connections` | `Iterable[str]` | `()` | Names of connections of the environment the asset reads from; each must exist when you deploy. Inside the task, `lakana.ingest.connections.get` reads one, with its secret. At most 16, each lower-case letters, digits and ``-``, starting with a letter. |
| `write` | `str` | `'replace'` | ``replace`` (the default): every run replaces the table's rows with what the function returns. ``append``: the first run creates the table; each later run adds the rows it returns, and needs `watermark`. ``merge``: rows whose `key` matches a row of the table update it, the others are added; nothing is deleted. Needs `key`. |
| `key` | `Iterable[str] | str` | `()` | The columns that identify a row: a list, or one string for a key of one column. It is also the key of ``write="merge"``. ``"none"`` says that no columns identify a row; only for ``kind="fact"`` or ``kind="wide"``, never with ``merge``. |
| `watermark` | `str | None` | `None` | The column whose largest value in the table the next run starts after: needed by ``write="append"``, optional for ``merge``. |
| `evolve_schema` | `bool | None` | `False` | ``False`` (the default): a run whose result has other columns or types than the table fails, and the table stays as it is. ``True``: each run's replace lets the table take the schema the function returns: new columns are added, a column whose type widens (``Int32`` to ``Int64``, ``Float32`` to ``Float64``) keeps its data, a column whose type changes otherwise becomes a new column (its earlier values read as null), and a column the result no longer has is removed from the table. Only with ``write="replace"``; `None` means ``False``. |
| `valid_from` | `str | None` | `None` | For ``write="history"``: the column whose value is when a row's values took effect (a date or a timestamp); without it a new version starts when the run began. |
| `close_missing` | `bool | None` | `None` | For ``write="history"``: close the open version of a key the function no longer returns. Never deletes. |
| `kind` | `str | None` | `None` | ``fact``, ``dimension``, ``wide`` or ``staging``. A fact and a wide table need `grain` and `key`; a dimension needs `grain` and a real `key`; a staging table needs nothing. Not allowed with ``output="artifact"``. |
| `grain` | `str | None` | `None` | One line, at most 300 characters, saying what one row is. |
| `references` | `Mapping[str, str | Mapping[str, str]] | None` | `None` | Column of this table → the table it refers to, as ``ns.table`` (that table's single key column) or ``ns.table.column``; for a table that keeps history (``write="history"``), ``{"to": &lt;target&gt;, "at": &lt;the row's time column&gt;}``. |
| `checks` | `Mapping[str, str] | None` | `None` | Generated-check family (``key``, ``references``, ``measures``) → ``block``, ``keep`` or ``warn``: what a failure does. |
| `measures` | `Mapping[str, Mapping[str, object]] | None` | `None` | Column → its measure: ``aggregation`` (required), ``additivity``, ``not_over``, ``unit`` or ``currency``, ``label``, ``description``; only with ``kind`` ``fact`` or ``wide``. Not allowed with ``output="artifact"``. |
| `health` | `str | bool | Mapping[str, object] | None` | `None` | Health signals to warn on, block on or switch off: ``"off"``, or a dict such as ``{"volume": "block", "range": {"price": "off"}}``; see the table health reference. Not allowed with ``output="artifact"``. |

Returns: `callable`. A decorator that sets `ASSET_ATTRIBUTE` on the function.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `TypeError` | For ``@asset`` without parentheses. |
| `ValueError` | For an `output` other than ``table`` or ``artifact``, a `materialize` other than ``table``, `materialize` or `columns` on an artifact asset, and a `keep_versions` that is not an integer from 1 to 2147483647 or that is given without ``output="artifact"``, a `decimals` other than ``float`` or ``exact``, a `connections` that is not a list of valid, distinct names or holds more than 16, a `write`, `key` or `watermark` deploy would refuse (also any of them on an artifact asset), an `evolve_schema` that is not a boolean, or is ``True`` on an artifact asset or with an append, a merge or a history write, ``write="history"`` without ``kind="dimension"``, a `valid_from` or `close_missing` that deploy would refuse, and a `kind`, `grain`, `references`, `checks`, `measures` or `health` deploy would refuse (also any of them on an artifact asset). |

## `lakana.output_dir`

Signature: `lakana.output_dir() -> Path`

Return the directory an artifact asset writes its files into.

The function writes a file or a tree here and returns its path: a file inside this directory, or the directory itself (or a subdirectory).

The directory is available from the import of the asset's module until the upload has ended, so a call at module level works too; it is meant for the asset function.

Returns: `pathlib.Path`. An empty, private directory of this task attempt.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `RuntimeError` | Outside a task, and in a task whose asset produces a table. |
